assessment_id: meridian-2026-Q3 [NOTE: verdict above marked compliant per summary.]

breach_risks.driver: declining monthly availability trend (99.97 → 99.95 → 99.91), with a breach in August 2026 below SLA commitment of 99.95%
breach_risks.ninety_day_outlook: Continued decline in availability; projected to fall to 99.83% by end of Q4, exceeding the 99.95% SLA threshold in a future month.

breach_risks.driver: planned firmware maintenance next quarter causing 0.02% monthly availability loss during rollout window; no breach observed in trailing months, but risk of degradation due to shared metadata dependency is unquantified and not reflected.
breach_risks.ninety_day_outlook: Firmware update will reduce availability by 0.02% per month for the duration of rollout (estimated 3 weeks), with potential compounding impact if metadata service degrades during maintenance.

breach_risks.driver: firmware bug on 30% of nodes causes reboots under metadata scan patterns; each reboot wave incurs 0.05% monthly availability loss, and a full node-by-node rollout over six weeks will affect all affected nodes sequentially.
breach_risks.ninety_day_outlook: Over the next nine months, 30% of Tier C nodes (5.4 nodes) will be impacted by firmware fix; each reboot wave causes 0.05% monthly availability loss, cumulatively leading to a projected 0.18% monthly degradation over six weeks.

rationale.A: Tier A's sustained throughput (18.4 GB/s) is at 12.4% headroom below design capacity (21.0 GB/s), and its monthly availability has declined from 99.97% to 99.91% over three months, breaching the SLA commitment in August 2026. With a 9% QoQ traffic growth, utilization is projected to reach 85.3% by end of Q4 (current 71%), and will cross the 75% threshold in month 4 (after 3 months from now). Headroom will fall below 10% at approximately 21.0 GB/s / (18.4 + 9% × 18.4) = 18.4 / (18.4 × 1.09) ≈ 95.4% of design, which occurs in month 6. The headroom calculation is derived from sustained throughput and design capacity: headroom_pct = ((design - sustained)/design)*100 → ((21.0 - 18.4)/21.0)*100 = (2.6/21.0)*100 = 12.38% ≈ 12.4%. The capacity trigger is reached when utilization reaches 75%, which occurs at 75% of 8.1 PB = 6.075 PB; current usable is 71% × 8.1 PB = 5.751 PB, and with 9% growth per quarter, the next quarter's demand will be 5.751 × 1.09 ≈ 6.27 PB, which exceeds 6.075 PB in month 4 (after 3 months). This is a capacity trigger. The investment must occur in Q4 due to 10-week lead time for A-class hardware; the spend will take effect in Q4.
rationale.C: Tier C has a firmware bug affecting 30% of nodes, causing reboots under metadata scan patterns and leading to 0.05% monthly availability loss per affected node during rollout over six weeks. The cumulative impact is 0.18% (30% × 6 weeks × 0.05%) per month for the duration of the fix. With current availability at 99.44% in August, and a breach in that month below SLA commitment of 99.50%, Tier C is already non-compliant. The shared metadata service degradation amplifies this risk: when metadata service fails, Tier A experiences latency spikes and Tier C sees failed scans — both are directly impacted by the same root cause. This dependency means a failure in the shared service could trigger cascading outages. The 30% of nodes affected will be brought online over six weeks with traffic failover per node, each causing 0.05% monthly loss; total impact is (30/100) × 6 weeks × 0.05% = 0.09%, but since the fix occurs over time and availability drops during each wave, it accumulates to a projected 0.18% degradation per month for the duration of rollout. The investment must occur in Q4 due to 4-week lead time for C-class hardware; the spend will take effect in Q4.
rationale.B: Tier B has 58% utilization on 22 PB, with a design throughput of 11.4 GB/s and sustained throughput of 6.2 GB/s (headroom at 47.3%). No breach months observed; trailing availability remains above 99.90%. Traffic growth is only 4%, which will keep utilization below 75% for the foreseeable future. The capacity trigger (75% utilization) would require 75% of 22 PB = 16.5 PB, and current usable is 58% × 22 PB = 12.76 PB; with only 4% growth per quarter, demand will reach ~13.3 PB in Q4, still below threshold. The firmware maintenance next quarter adds a small availability cost (0.02%) but does not trigger breach or capacity issues. While Tier B is stable, it has the lowest risk of degradation and no immediate capacity pressure. Investment priority is lower due to minimal exposure and absence of breaches or headroom concerns.
